comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense decreased $2.4 billion to $1.7 billion, primarily due to the absence of a $2.1 billion prior-year accrual for the FDIC special assessment following the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, along with lower expenses from liquidating business activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclosed FDIC special assessment impacts in their 2024 results, but the timing and nature of the expenses differed. JPM recorded a $725 million increase to the accrual in Q1 2024 based on revised loss estimates, adding to the $2.9 billion assessed in late 2023. In contrast, Bank of America's 2024 noninterest expense decrease was primarily driven by the absence of a $2.1 billion accrual recorded in the prior year (2023) for the special assessment related to SVB and Signature Bank closures, indicating BAC's major assessment hit occurred in 2023 while JPM's incremental adjustment occurred in 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: All Other (managed basis) expenses decreased 19%, largely due to lower FDIC special assessments ($203 million vs $1.7 billion) and reduced restructuring charges ($259 million vs $781 million), partially offset by civil money penalties imposed in July 2024; cost of credit decreased to $1.1 billion from $1.3 billion, driven by a smaller ACL build for non-U.S. transfer risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup reported FDIC special assessment expenses for 2024, highlighting a trend of declining annual charges compared to prior years. JPM reported a $725 million increase to the assessment in Q1 2024 following a large $2.9 billion assessment in Q4 2023. Citigroup reported significantly lower FDIC special assessments in 2024 ($203 million) compared to the prior year ($1.7 billion), attributing the decrease to the passage of the initial large assessment period. Both disclosures illustrate that while assessments continued in 2024, the magnitude was lower for C than the incremental adjustment faced by JPM.

sentences.text: (e)The first quarter of 2024 included an increase of $725 million to the FDIC special assessment reflecting the FDIC's revised estimate of Deposit Insurance Fund losses.

All Other (managed basis) expenses decreased 19%, primarily driven by the lower FDIC special assessment ($203 million in 2024 versus approximately $1.7 billion in the prior year) and a reduction from the closed exits and wind-downs, as well as the lower restructuring charges ($259 million in 2024 versus $781 million in 2023), partially offset by the civil money penalties imposed by the FRB and OCC in July 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors driving 2024 operating expense decreases and increases
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased relative to 2023 due to lower commercial real estate impairments, GreenSky intangible asset write-downs, consumer platform goodwill impairments, and FDIC fees, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction-based expenses driven by improved performance. An additional $71 million FDIC special assessment fee was recognized in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs identified the FDIC special assessment as a specific line-item expense in 2024, contributing to their operating expense variances. JPM recognized a $725 million increase to the special assessment in Q1 2024 due to revised FDIC loss estimates. Goldman Sachs recognized an incremental expense of $71 million for the FDIC special assessment fee in 2024, also noting that this fee was driven by the FDIC's updated cost estimates from the 2023 bank closures. Unlike JPM's larger incremental accrual, GS's 2024 charge was a smaller incremental fee relative to the total operating expense context.

sentences.text: (e)The first quarter of 2024 included an increase of $725 million to the FDIC special assessment reflecting the FDIC's revised estimate of Deposit Insurance Fund losses.

An incremental expense for the FDIC special assessment fee of $71 million was recognized in 2024, as the FDIC notified banks subject to the special assessment fee of the updated estimated cost to the Deposit Insurance Fund resulting from the closures in 2023 of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Non-Interest Expense Trend and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management non-interest expenses increased 5% to $20,618 million in 2024 compared to the prior year. This increase was driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses, primarily due to increased formulaic payouts to representatives on higher compensable revenues, partially offset by decreases in non-compensation expenses such as professional services, legal expenses, and FDIC special assessment costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley included FDIC special assessments in their 2024 expense discussions, though the context differed. JPM disclosed a specific $725 million increase to the assessment accrual in Q1 2024. Morgan Stanley mentioned 'lower FDIC special assessment cost' as a factor reducing non-compensation expenses in its Wealth Management segment, indicating that the assessment burden was decreasing or lower than in prior periods for MS, whereas JPM was actively increasing its accrual based on revised estimates.
